title: Calling a Deer a Horse
synopsis: “Calling a Deer a Horse” is a Chinese idiom originating from the Qin dynasty.

fullText.simplified:
指鹿为马

    “指鹿为马”是一个成语，意思是“指着鹿，说是马”。这个成语出自司马迁的《史记》。
    秦朝丞相赵高想要造反，怕其他大臣不服气，不听他的话，就想了一个办法来试一试大家。他拉来一只鹿给皇帝，说：“这是一匹马。”皇帝笑着说：“丞相，你弄错了吧？这是一只鹿。”赵高就问旁边的大臣们这到底是鹿还是马？大臣们有的不说话，有的说是鹿，有的跟着赵高说是马。说是鹿的人，后来都被赵高杀了。从此以后，大臣们都很怕赵高。
    现在，人们用“指鹿为马”来比喻故意歪曲事实，颠倒黑白。你可以说：“我们都要做正直的人，不能指鹿为马。”
fullText.traditional:
指鹿為馬

    “指鹿為馬”是一個成語，意思是“指著鹿，說是馬”。這個成語出自司馬遷的《史記》。
    秦朝丞相趙高想要造反，怕其他大臣不服氣，不聽他的話，就想了一個辦法來試一試大家。他拉來一隻鹿給皇帝，說：“這是一匹馬。”皇帝笑著說：“丞相，你弄錯了吧？這是一隻鹿。”趙高就問旁邊的大臣們這到底是鹿還是馬？大臣們有的不說話，有的說是鹿，有的跟著趙高說是馬。說是鹿的人，後來都被趙高殺了。從此以後，大臣們都很怕趙高。
    現在，人們用“指鹿為馬”來比喻故意歪曲事實，顛倒黑白。你可以說：“我們都要做正直的人，不能指鹿為馬。”

raw.synopsis: “Calling a Deer a Horse” is a Chinese idiom originating from the Qin dynasty.
sentence_translations: “Calling a Deer a Horse” is an idiom which means “To point at a deer, and say it is a horse”.
This idiom comes from Sima Qian’s “Records of the Grand Historian”.
The senior minister in the Qin dynasty, Zhao Gao, wanted to make a revolt, ..
.. but was afraid that the other ministers would dismiss and not listen to him.
So he came up with a method for testing everyone.
He pulled out a deer in front of the emperor, and said: “This is a horse.”
The emperor laughed and said: “Senior minister, you must be mistaken? This is a deer.”
Zhao Gao then asked the ministers next to him: “Is this a deer or a horse?”
Some ministers didn’t answer, some said it was a deer, and some followed Zhao Gao in saying it was a horse.
Afterwards, everyone who said it was a deer was killed by Zhao Gao.
From that onwards, all the ministers were afraid of Zhao Gao.
Nowadays, people use “Calling a Deer a Horse” to describe deliberately bending facts, and distorting the truth.
You can say: “We should all be honest people, and not call a deer a horse.”
